meta.tagline: One roster gap. One call at a time. Stop at the first yes.
notes: CALL-E caps the video at 3 minutes. Target 2:45 assembled including cards; 178s is the wall.
The held beat is b5 - the moment the cascade stops. Everything before it exists to make that land.
Every transcript on screen is AUTHORED - written by scripts/make-fixtures.mjs, not recorded from anyone. No real call appears in this video.
Narration never reads an identifier aloud. Ids and hashes stay on screen and out of the script.

beats.name: The problem
beats.screen: Landing screen, still. The gap panel on the left, the standby list waiting.

narration.text: Five forty in the morning. A care home is one nurse short.
Somebody now rings twenty casual staff, one at a time, until one says yes.
One at a time - because ring all twenty and four say yes, and now you have to un-invite three people who already got out of bed.

beats.name: What it will not do
beats.screen: The withheld-capability panel on the right.

narration.text: This agent telephones real people about work, before dawn.
So it states on its own front page what it may not do.
Not call in parallel. Not negotiate pay. Not ring anyone the employer did not put on the roster.

beats.name: One gap, ten people
beats.screen: The gap: the shift, the note, the standby list of ten.

narration.text: Here is the gap. Early care shift, six o'clock, two residents who need two people to lift them.
Ten on the standby list. Watch who never gets rung.

beats.name: The cascade runs
beats.screen: Live: skips, then calls resolving one at a time.

narration.text: Two are skipped before anything is dialled - one opted out, one has no number on file. Both with the reason recorded.
Then it dials. One person at a time, never two.
No answer. A refusal. Somebody asking to be rung back in twenty minutes.

beats.name: And it stops
beats.screen: The accept lands. Everyone below goes grey.

narration.text: The fifth call says yes, arriving at ten to six.
And the cascade stops.
Four people below the line are stood down and never rung - recorded, with the reason.

beats.name: The transcript behind it
beats.screen: Click the accepting call; the transcript panel opens.

narration.text: Every outcome opens the call behind it: the goal the agent was given, and what was said.
The transcripts are written, not recorded - so this runs with no account, and no one's phone call in it.

beats.name: Reading the answer
beats.screen: Back to the list; the declined and callback rows.

narration.text: Reading that answer has three outcomes, not two.
This one is a clear no, so the cascade moves on. A call nobody could read does not - it stops, and waits for a person to say what it meant.
One call here reached voicemail. The provider calls that completed, because a message was delivered. It is not a person agreeing to come in at six.

beats.name: When nobody can
beats.screen: Re-run with the nobody-available scenario; it exhausts and says so.

narration.text: When nobody can take it, it says so and stops.
It does not loop, does not widen the list, does not ring anyone twice. A human decides what happens to the shift.

beats.name: Proved without a phone
beats.screen: Back on the landing screen, capability panel in shot.

narration.text: The rule that matters is not a comment: a second call in flight raises an error. So does dialling while a call is held for a person.
That, the retry pass and the stop condition are sixty-three assertions against a state machine with no phone.
No CALL-E account? Install nothing, sign up for nothing. Run npm start.
The whole product runs offline in thirty seconds, with no account at all.
Standby. One gap, one call at a time, stop at the first yes.
